approachQuestion.prompt:
Relative sign totals. Each inclusive query [l,r] asks for a[l]-a[l+1]+a[l+2]-... with the first sign always positive. Return q answers.

Input: a=[3,5,2,7], queries [[1,3],[0,2]]. Output: [10,0].

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ l ≤ r < n; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000; sums fit 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build P[k] as the sum of (-1)^i*a[i] over i<k. For [l,r], subtract P[l] from P[r+1] and negate the result exactly when l is odd.
options.feedback: The global sign convention differs from the query convention by the sign at its left endpoint.
For a=[3,5] and [1,1], it returns -5 instead of 5.

options.text: Walk each requested range, alternating the sign from positive.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

The prepared alternating signs are tied to global index parity. An odd left endpoint reverses every desired local sign, so negate the prefix difference for exactly that case.

Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

feedback.reason: One signed prefix array and a parity check suffice per request.
details: The table costs O(n) entries and one pass; every query uses constant work.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

One pass creates n+1 signed prefix totals. Each query then performs two reads, a subtraction, and at most one negation, all constant-time 64-bit operations. This gives O(n+q). O(nq) would rescan and alternate signs across every queried range instead of reusing the prepared totals.

The allocated prefix table has n+1 entries, independent of the number q of requests. Auxiliary space is therefore O(n), not O(1) and not O(q): q may be small while n is large. Query answers are required output and excluded; the prefix table and fixed scalar temporaries are working storage.
